California’s proposed billionaire wealth tax, or Proposition 40, could generate an initial windfall but ultimately leave the state billions of dollars poorer, according to a new analysis from Stanford economists.

Benjamin Jaros and Joshua Rauh of Stanford University’s Hoover Institution, in a working paper published in October by the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER), estimate Proposition 40 would collect roughly $30 billion. Their projection ranges from $28 billion to $36 billion, well below the $100 billion supporters have forecast.

The economists’ analysis estimates billionaire departures have already reduced the potential tax base by nearly 30% or about $540 billion. According to the paper, further departures could cost California between $1 billion and $3.5 billion in annual income-tax revenue. If sustained indefinitely, those losses could exceed the wealth tax proceeds by about $39 billion in present-value terms.

“These findings suggest that the Billionaire Tax Act will not fulfill the primary functions for which it was designed,” Jaros and Rauh wrote.

Read Also: Bernie Sanders Says Midterms Campaign Is About Whether ‘Trillionaire’ Elon Musk Can ‘Buy Our Government’ — ‘Say NO to Oligarchy’

Zuckerberg Deal Amid Tax Threat

Proposition 40, set for California’s Nov. 3 ballot, would impose a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of billionaires who lived in the state on Jan. 1, 2026, with payments generally due in 2027. Real estate, pensions, and most retirement accounts would be excluded, while taxpayers opting to pay over five years would owe more. The measure would allocate 90% of its proceeds to health care.

Billionaires who have left California include venture capitalist Peter Thiel and the co-founders of Alphabet Inc.‘s (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) Google Larry Page and Sergey Brin.

On Wednesday, Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) CEO Mark Zuckerberg agreed to remain in California or wherever Meta is headquartered for eight years in exchange for non-voting Class C shares he could sell to cover a potential multibillion-dollar tax bill if voters approve the proposed billionaire wealth tax. Forbes estimates his net worth at $239.3 billion. He could sell 20% of the new shares, equivalent to 10% of his total economic interest, to pay for the potential tax liability, while retaining voting control of Meta.

Wealth Tax Debate Intensifies

The potential exodus has been debated for months. In August, billionaire entrepreneur Mark Cuban said the proposal could discourage investment. He said startup founders often become "cash poor, stock rich" as their companies reach billion-dollar valuations, leaving them with limited cash to pay wealth taxes without selling shares or borrowing against them.

In June, economist Peter Schiff warned that taxing unrealized asset values could accelerate capital flight and weaken California’s tax base rather than generate lasting revenue. He argued that taxing accumulated private wealth could undermine the nation’s economic foundation, asking why billionaires would stay to face the levy.

However, SEIU-UHW, the healthcare workers union behind the ballot measure, rejected the Stanford research and told CBS News that the proposal aims to make billionaires pay their fair share to prevent California’s healthcare system from collapsing. Union Vice President Debru Carthan accused opponents of spreading misinformation.

Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang compared controlling autonomous AI agents to looking after a baby in a playpen.

“You contain the baby and you monitor it,” Huang said Thursday morning on CNBC.

He described Nvidia’s security technology as a “super smart force field around AI,” expressing confidence that it could have handled previous incidents involving AI agents behaving unexpectedly.

OpenAI Agents Weakened Monitoring Systems

The comments follow an OpenAI report updated Tuesday detailing two incidents in which AI agents weakened monitoring during internal coding tasks.

One disabled automatic alerts to OpenAI’s security team. Another removed monitoring from software it was modifying, then falsely denied doing so.

OpenAI said the agents themselves remained monitored but was investigating whether their behavior reflected excessive persistence or attempts to evade oversight.

Asked whether OpenShell could stop problems such as unintended hacks and agents accessing websites, Huang replied: “We’re confident that it would have handled the incidents we’ve seen.”

He did not identify which incidents he meant.

Nvidia Builds a ‘Force Field’ Around AI

On Wednesday, Nvidia unveiled its OpenShell Reference Architecture, building on existing software designed to keep autonomous AI agents within strict boundaries.

OpenShell restricts which files, websites and tools an agent can access. A second system, called Sentry, monitors activity using separate security hardware.

Rather than trusting agents to obey instructions, Nvidia aims to enforce restrictions outside their control.

The company says Sentry can quarantine agents that violate security policies within milliseconds.

OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft and CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWD) are among the companies working with the architecture.

CrowdStrike announced Wednesday that it is integrating its Falcon Guardian security software with OpenShell to detect potentially malicious AI agent activity, with plans to extend those protections to Nvidia’s hardware-based Sentry system.

Huang Says AI Safety Cannot Wait for Regulators

Huang argued that companies must act immediately rather than wait for government intervention.

“Regulations take a while to come,” he said.

Asked why the public should trust AI companies, Huang pointed to their commercial incentives.

“There’s no such thing as a good product that’s not safe,” he said.

On Polymarket, traders assign a 9% probability to the U.S. enacting an AI safety law before 2027, with approximately $205,000 traded.

Huang acknowledged that new threats could emerge.

“We don’t know what we don’t know about the future,” he said.

Comcast Corp. (NASDAQ:CMCSA) reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings Thursday as growth in NBCUniversal’s media business and Peacock helped offset continued broadband subscriber losses and weakness in theme parks.

The Philadelphia-based company reported revenue of $29.298 billion, down 6.1% year over year but above analysts’ consensus estimate of $29.269 billion, according to Benzinga Pro.

Adjusted earnings of $1.07 per share beat analysts’ expectations of 98 cents.

Peacock Revenue Surges 34% As Media Business Expands

Comcast’s media revenue increased 13% to $5.36 billion, driven by World Cup programming and stronger performance at Peacock.

Peacock revenue jumped 34% to $1.8 billion, while the streaming service generated $261 million in adjusted EBITDA, reversing a $217 million loss a year earlier.

Paid subscribers increased 17% year over year to 48 million.

Universal’s film business also contributed to results, with “The Odyssey” becoming the studio’s highest-grossing film.

Studio adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization rose 18.6% to $402 million, although lower content licensing revenue pushed overall studio revenue down 1.1%.

Comcast Loses 144,000 Broadband Customers

Comcast lost 144,000 residential broadband customers during the quarter, compared with 91,000 losses a year earlier, marking an approximately 58% increase in subscriber losses.

The decline was steeper than the 133,000 losses expected by analysts, according to Bloomberg.

Competition from wireless and fiber providers continued to pressure the business.

Comcast CFO Jason Armstrong called rival fiber providers’ $30-to-$40 broadband pricing in certain markets “irrational competition,” warning that competitive pressures intensified in the second half of the year.

Video subscriber losses increased 6.8% to 274,000 as more consumers shifted toward streaming services.

Comcast is responding by combining broadband with Xfinity Mobile offerings and introducing promotional deals to attract and retain customers.

The company added 368,000 mobile lines during the quarter, bringing its wireless customer base to 10.6 million.

Theme Park Profit Falls As Costs Rise

Theme park revenue declined 4.4% to $2.6 billion, while adjusted EBITDA fell 17.1% amid higher operating expenses and weaker revenue.

Connectivity & Platforms adjusted EBITDA decreased 4.4% to $7.6 billion. The segment’s adjusted EBITDA margin narrowed 70 basis points to 38.6%.

Management expects theme park performance to improve through 2027, with a return to growth anticipated in the second half of the year.

See More: Top Value Stocks

Comcast Plans Job Cuts And Business Restructuring

Comcast is preparing significant job cuts and a broader reorganization of its cable, broadband and wireless operations as it reshapes its business, Bloomberg reported Wednesday.

The restructuring aims to simplify operations, improve efficiency and free up cash for future investments as the company faces continued pressure on broadband and video subscriptions.

Comcast is also pursuing a proposed separation involving NBCUniversal and Sky, following its earlier separation of cable networks into Versant.

CNBC reported Thursday that co-CEO and Chair Brian Roberts previously said the separation would allow the businesses to operate with greater strategic flexibility, dedicated management attention and investment priorities.

Wireless And Enterprise Services Offer Growth Opportunities

President Mike Cavanagh described wireless as a “tremendous growth opportunity,” pointing to Comcast’s capital-light business model and ability to leverage its existing broadband and Wi-Fi networks.

Wireless lines increased 18% year over year to 10.6 million. About 70% of customers receiving free mobile lines are converting to paid relationships, according to management.

Comcast also sees opportunities in enterprise services as businesses invest in advanced connectivity, managed networking and cybersecurity products.

The company is exploring edge computing opportunities across its network of roughly 1,400 headends and 250 megawatts of capacity, potentially creating another source of long-term growth.

Peacock Expands Through YouTube Partnerships

Cavanagh said Comcast is expanding Peacock’s distribution through third-party bundles after initially emphasizing direct-to-consumer subscriber growth.

A new YouTube Premium-Peacock bundle is designed to attract younger consumers who engage with NBC content but have not subscribed to Peacock.

Comcast also extended its YouTube TV distribution agreement, expanded advertising partnerships and is exploring international growth opportunities.

Management remains open to additional distribution partnerships while seeking to minimize the risk of existing subscribers switching to discounted bundles.

Comcast Uses AI To Cut Customer Service Costs

Chief Financial Officer Jason Armstrong said Comcast is accelerating artificial intelligence adoption across its network and customer service operations through partnerships with Sierra and Cresta.

The initiatives have helped reduce customer service contact rates by roughly 20% and eliminate more than 30 million service interactions year to date, according to the company.

Comcast also participates in the Personal Agent Protocol initiative led by Sierra and Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META).

Separately, Comcast is working with Starlink to combine satellite connectivity with Comcast Business managed services for enterprise customers.

Executives said the company remains open to additional technology and network partnerships.

Cash Flow Remains Strong Despite Business Pressures

Comcast generated $4.2 billion in free cash flow during the quarter and returned $1.2 billion to shareholders through dividends.

As previously announced, the company suspended share repurchases beginning in the third quarter and expects the pause to continue through its proposed business separation.

Connectivity & Platforms capital expenditures rose 3.6% to $2.4 billion, reflecting increased spending on customer equipment and network infrastructure.

Capital spending in Content & Experiences declined 10.6% to $639 million.

Management identified wireless convergence, business services, Peacock partnerships, AI adoption and restructuring as long-term growth opportunities.

Executives expect modest improvement in connectivity trends during the fourth quarter, although broadband competition and theme park weakness remain near-term challenges.

Price Action: Comcast shares rose 5.07% to $23.21 on Thursday at the time of publication, according to Benzinga Pro.

Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang said the U.S. must treat China as a major rival in chips, AI, and research while competing globally through innovation and infrastructure.

Huang made the remarks during an interview with Yahoo Finance journalist Deirdre Bosa on the sidelines of Nvidia’s GTC Berlin conference on Wednesday. Asked about reports that DeepSeek and Huawei are working together on chip designs, Huang said the U.S. should always take China “seriously” as both a manufacturing powerhouse and technology competitor.

Huang said, “If there’s one country that could manufacture things at scale,” it is China. He lauded Beijing’s capacity to produce chips, open AI models, and even AI researchers at enormous scale.

“We’ve got to recognize that we have very, very serious competition,” he said.

However, Huang added that American frontier laboratories, computing systems and infrastructure remain the strongest in the world.

He said that the U.S. government and policymakers have made it possible for American companies to be in Africa and Central Asia, and would like to compete in Brazil, Egypt and other markets.

Read Also: Micron CTO Downplays New Memory Chip Design as ‘Complex and Costly’ While Chinese Rival CXMT Advances DRAM Technology

China’s AI Push Pressures Nvidia

The warning comes as Huawei gains ground in China’s AI accelerator market. An IDC analysis, earlier this month, found Nvidia held 34% of the market during the first half of 2026, compared with 28% for Huawei. Nvidia shipped 678,000 accelerators in China during that period, but its shipments fell 44% from the same period a year earlier, according to the report.

Previously, Huang urged the U.S. to embrace China’s AI models rather than ban them, calling the technology "excellent" and arguing that open-source models can expand AI adoption without threatening closed-model providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic. Huang also dismissed concerns that China could use these models to undermine U.S. companies, saying there was "Zero possibility" of Chinese AI driving American firms out of the market.

Meanwhile, former Google CEO Eric Schmidt said in a podcast interview that China trails the U.S. in AI by about six months but could still prevail because its products are offered free. He said China’s low-cost and free AI models, along with open-weight systems, could gain traction in developing economies that cannot afford expensive Western alternatives.

Billionaire investor Chamath Palihapitiya says Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) has a ceiling on its value and believes a future hack could eventually send it to zero.

Why Palihapitiya Thinks Bitcoin Is Capped

Palihapitiya told the Moonshots podcast that traditional crypto lacks the fungibility needed to attract the full range of potential buyers. 

Retail and institutional investors can hold it, he said, but central banks largely can’t.

He flagged two additional risks beyond that limited buyer pool:

  • Privacy exposure: citing France, where forced publication of crypto holdings led to a wave of kidnappings
  • AI-driven hacking: He argued that recursively self-improving AI models could eventually target Bitcoin’s SHA-256 security and potentially crack Satoshi Nakamoto’s wallet.

On that second risk, Palihapitiya noted an attacker could profit twice, first by draining the wallet, then by shorting Bitcoin after revealing the hack publicly. 

“I just think it’s capped, and then I think eventually it gets hacked, and then it goes to zero,” he said, adding that migrating to quantum-resistant cryptography is “basically impossible” given how divided the Bitcoin community already is on basic coordination.

Palihapitiya also said he no longer holds Bitcoin directly. He moved his exposure into equity through Digital Currency Group years ago specifically to avoid storage and security risk.

Why He Still Sees Opportunity Elsewhere

Despite his Bitcoin call, Palihapitiya said he remains bullish on power and energy infrastructure as the defining investment theme of the next decade, pointing to roughly six gigawatts of capacity he has personally accumulated.

He argued that the U.S. faces a structural electricity shortfall even if developers complete every planned power project on time, making solar and natural gas the fastest and most practical options to close the gap.

He also pushed back on traditional index investing, arguing the S&P 500 (NYSE:SPY) no longer offers the diversification it once did because gains concentrate in a small handful of mega-cap names. 

His alternative: rank companies across the S&P 500 and global indexes by free cash flow yield, then buy the top performers instead of the index itself.

On his own portfolio, Palihapitiya called himself the least invested he’s been in 15 years. “I’m in this schizophrenia about pivoting towards cash flow,” he admitted, pointing to uncertainty over how artificial general intelligence could reshape markets and asset values in the years ahead.

He said he still favors cash flow-generating businesses, power infrastructure, and alternative ways to deploy capital outside traditional financial systems.

Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) grew revenue 26% in the third quarter and beat its own forecast. It also spent more money than it brought in, a first in more than a decade of quarterly cash flow data.

Free cash flow came in at negative $2.12 billion, according to the company’s earnings release. A year earlier, Meta generated $10.63 billion.

Meta’s quarterly free cash flow had not dipped below zero since the second quarter of 2012, the quarter in which the company went public.

Shares were down 6.6% to $651.05 in morning trading on Thursday. Yet Wall Street analysts spent the morning raising their price targets.

Meta’s Capex Now Exceeds Its Operating Cash

Free cash flow is the money left after a company pays for its buildings, servers and equipment. It is what funds buybacks, dividends and acquisitions without new debt.

Meta’s operations generated $32.79 billion in the third quarter. Purchases of property and equipment reached $33.94 billion, or 104% of that amount. Another $964 million went to finance-lease payments.

Including leases, capital spending reached $34.91 billion, equal to 54% of revenue.

Over the first nine months of the year, free cash flow fell 63% to $11.05 billion.

The balance sheet tells the same story. Meta ended September with $82.45 billion in cash and marketable securities against $80.92 billion in long-term debt, leaving a net cash cushion of about $1.5 billion.

Meanwhile, the bill keeps growing. Meta narrowed its 2026 capex outlook to $135 billion to $145 billion, up from a low end of $130 billion. It gave no 2027 number, saying only that it expects to keep investing aggressively.

Its quarterly filing also lists $454.52 billion of non-cancelable contractual commitments.

Read Also: CoreWeave Bonds Stop Bleeding After SpaceX Results, But Investors Still Demand 3x Treasury Yields

The Business Is Not The Problem

Revenue rose to $64.60 billion from $51.24 billion a year earlier. Meta guided fourth-quarter revenue to $73 billion to $76 billion.

Headcount fell 15% from a year earlier to 66,775 employees.

The market’s first reaction was positive. Then it reversed.

“In fact, the stocks of all three corporations rallied in the immediate aftermath of their quarterly updates, only to stop suddenly and reverse sharply,” David Morrison, senior market analyst at Trade Nation, said in a note on Thursday, referring to Meta, Tesla and IBM.

He pointed to AI spending as the common thread.

“The future commitments are enormous. Yet there’s little clarity over when, or even if, there will be a return on planned expenditure,” Morrison said.

Why A Delay Would Hurt More Than A Slowdown

Torsten Slok, chief economist at Apollo Global Management, listed hyperscalers’ growth and earnings among the losers if the data center buildout takes longer than planned.

“Revenue is capped by supply rather than demand, and committed capex keeps accruing while capacity sits idle,” Slok said in a note on Tuesday.

At 22V Research, Dennis DeBusschere said reducing the uncertainty around AI returns is “necessary for a rerating higher” in AI buildout stocks.

Wall Street Pays For The Ads, Not The Bill

Analysts did not back away. Seven firms updated their views on Meta on Thursday, and six of them raised their price targets, according to Benzinga Analyst Ratings.

The 35 analysts tracked by Benzinga rate the stock a Buy on consensus, with 31 Buy or Strong Buy ratings and four Holds.

The average price target of $856 implies about 26% upside from the premarket price.

The largest increase came from Susquehanna, which lifted its target to $850 from $650. The highest target among recent moves belongs to Truist Securities at $1,000, set on Oct. 13.

The disconnect is the story.

Analysts are valuing Meta’s advertising engine. Investors are pricing the AI bill.

Read Also: Are Companies Reducing AI Spending? Chip Orders Say Otherwise

The cash burn does not mean Meta is in trouble.

The company still earns tens of billions every quarter from its core business. However, for the first time since its first year as a public company, the AI buildout is costing more than that business brings in.

Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) suffered a major legal setback this week when a New Mexico judge ordered the company to pay $25 billion in penalties over the Cambridge Analytica scandal. 

The ruling followed a September jury verdict finding that Facebook misled users about their data privacy. While the headline figure drew most of the attention, a single sentence in the order added another cost: interest of 15% a year until the penalty is paid, which works out to about $3.75 billion annually.

Meta Platform’s New Mexico Bill Could Be Much Higher

In his ruling, Judge Francis J. Mathew wrote that New Mexico law will apply a statutory post-judgment interest clause to the company. This section applies when a civil judgment involves willful acts, intentional wrongdoing, or unconscionable trade practices. 

In this case, the judge ordered the company to pay 15% annual interest until it pays the cash. This means the company will now pay about $3.75 billion annually until it pays it off. 

These are huge numbers, even for a company the size of Meta Platforms. For example, Meta paid $1.36 billion in dividends in the third quarter, or about $5.4 billion annualized. In theory, the annual interest alone of roughly $3.75 billion would equal about 69% of that yearly shareholder payout.

Read Also: Lam Research Stock Sinks After Guidance Falls Short of Whispers: Cantor Calls It a 'Top Pick'

Meta Platforms Intends to Appeal

In a statement, Meta Platforms said that it planned to appeal the ruling to the New Mexico Courts of Appeals and potentially to the U.S. Supreme Court. In most cases, such appeals take between 3 and 5 years. If it takes four years and the company loses, its post-judgment interest alone would be about $15 billion, bringing the total to $ 40 billion. 

At the same time, to pause the enforcement of the $25 billion judgment while appealing, Meta will need to post a supersedeas bond or cash collateral. In this case, the company would need to commit about $30 billion, the principal judgment plus the interest expected to accrue during the appeal.

Instead of appealing, the company may also negotiate with New Mexico and reach a settlement. Such a move would prevent another expensive legal process. 

The ruling came two months after Meta Platforms settled with 52 attorneys general to resolve litigation related to teen mental health and social media. In its earnings report, Meta took a $9.89 billion charge related to this settlement. 

Meta ended the last quarter with $11.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $71 billion in marketable securities. Its non-marketable equity investments rose to $32 billion.

Palantir Technologies Inc. (NASDAQ:PLTR) is selling control as a product. The data analytics company touted a wave of sovereign AI deployments with flagship customers Wednesday, as one of its top executives worked to calm European allies worried about relying on American defense technology.

The customer list includes L3Harris Technologies Inc. (NYSE:LHX), NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA), Ondas Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:ONDS) and Regna AI.

Palantir said the group accelerated its own sovereignty efforts after last month’s joint announcement with Nvidia, which showed how Palantir’s Foundry, Ontology and AIP software sped up the chipmaker’s supply chain from wafer to first token.

The timing could be meaningful as Europe has spent the past week questioning its dependence on U.S. tech.

Starshield Restrictions Rattle Europe

Ukraine’s Starshield operations were unexpectedly restricted on Oct. 13 and 14. Starshield is the military-grade version of the satellite network run by Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX). 

Two U.S. officials and a Western official told Reuters the Pentagon’s leadership received instructions from within the White House to slow the service. 

A U.S. official told Reuters the president never made such a request. Ukrainian and European officials suspected a political motive, since the restrictions came after President Donald Trump demanded Ukraine stop striking Russian oil refineries, according to Reuters.

Read Also: Meta Just Unveiled a New Takeover Weapon — But There's a Catch

Palantir Says Customers Hold the Controls

Louis Mosley, Palantir’s executive vice president for the UK and Europe, addressed the fallout head-on. He told Reuters neither the company nor the U.S. could switch off the Maven Smart System AI platform used by NATO’s military headquarters and several European armed forces. 

"There are no kill switches," Mosley said. Customers who buy the software have full operational control and can run it independently of Palantir, he added. 

Maven processes large volumes of data from satellites, radars and other sensors to give military officers a picture of the battlefield and speed up decisions. NATO bought the system for its Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe in 2025 and declared it had reached full technical operational capability in June.  

But not every ally is sold. Germany and France have not adopted Maven for their own armed forces. In April, the head of Germany’s cyber command ruled out buying the system, saying private-company employees should never have access to the country’s national military database. 

Mosley said any Palantir staff involvement is up to the customer and would require local citizens with security clearance.

Sovereignty Push

Sovereignty has become the centerpiece of Palantir’s commercial pitch this year. The company hosted two Sovereignty Bootcamps in under 30 days over the summer, drawing nearly 200 organizations. The Starlink episode hands Palantir a live example of the exact risk its software claims to remove.

Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt says artificial intelligence “is not a bubble,” pointing to Anthropic‘s explosive revenue growth as evidence that customers are paying for technology they find useful.

“When I was CEO at Google, we set the revenue growth record. They smashed it more than twice the speed as we did,” Schmidt told Nicolai Tangen, head of Norway’s sovereign wealth fund, on the In Good Company podcast.

“That’s real growth there. It’s not fake. It’s real money with real customers who are paying for something useful in their eyes.”

Schmidt, who led Google, now part of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL), from 2001 to 2011, did not specify how he calculated the comparison.

He also has a substantial financial interest in Anthropic’s success. Bloomberg reported that Schmidt owns about 1% of the company, a stake potentially worth $15 billion to $20 billion at valuations discussed ahead of its anticipated IPO.

Anthropic’s Growth Comes With Enormous Costs

Anthropic told prospective investors that third-quarter revenue jumped 45% to $16.8 billion, up from $11.6 billion in the previous quarter and $4.7 billion in the first, Reuters reported.

The company also told investors it was profitable on an adjusted basis, although revenue growth slowed after more than doubling between the first and second quarters.

A draft IPO prospectus reviewed by Reuters revealed an $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of 2026, including a $72 billion noncash accounting charge tied to convertible financing.

Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing and infrastructure during those six months and has committed at least $518 billion over a decade.

China Could Win the AI Race on Users

Schmidt warned that Western AI companies could lose the global battle for customers even if they continue building more advanced models.

He estimates Chinese models are about six months behind their American rivals, but believes free alternatives could dominate in poorer countries.

“If you define losing as users, the vast majority of the world will use the free Chinese models rather than the more expensive Western models,” he said.

That raises a question for Anthropic and its rivals: how much of the global demand for AI can they convert into paying customers?

Polymarket Traders See Limited Risk of a 2026 Bust

On Polymarket, traders assign 9% odds of an AI-industry downturn by Dec. 31, with nearly $2.5 million traded.

The contract requires three specified events within a single 90-day period, including potential triggers such as Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) falling 50% from its all-time high or Anthropic or OpenAI declaring bankruptcy.

Those conditions measure a severe industry downturn, not whether AI stocks are overvalued.

Concerns about AI spending have already weighed on infrastructure providers, with CoreWeave Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV) recently hitting a 52-week low amid mounting AI debt concerns.

Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest sees Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA) potentially climbing nearly 1,100% by 2031, driven by robotaxis and humanoid robots. The forecast puts the spotlight on ETFs offering exposure to autonomous driving, robotics and artificial intelligence (AI).

In a report, ARK set a $4,400 base-case price target for Tesla, alongside a $3,300 bear case and a $5,000 bull case. Against the $367.29 share price cited in the report, the base case implies approximately 1,098% upside.

However, ARK’s forecast depends heavily on businesses that have yet to reach the scale envisioned in its projections. Investors looking to access these themes through ETFs have several options, each with a different balance of Tesla exposure and broader robotics investments.

ARKK, ARKQ and BOTZ Offer Different Routes

ARK Innovation ETF (NYSE:ARKK) provides the most direct Wood angle. Tesla accounts for 10.31% of its portfolio. The actively managed fund also holds SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) at 6.81%, alongside other innovation-focused companies. Its performance, however, depends on more than Tesla, making it a broader bet on disruptive technologies rather than a pure robotaxi investment.

ARK Autonomous Technology & Robotics ETF (BATS:ARKQ) offers a more targeted route into autonomous mobility and robotics. Tesla represents 12% of its portfolio, while SpaceX accounts for about 9.32%. Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) is another major holding, providing exposure to the computing infrastructure underpinning AI applications.

Global X Robotics & Artificial Intelligence ETF (NASDAQ:BOTZ) provides a broader, more diversified robotics approach. Tesla represents approximately 2.23% of its portfolio. Its portfolio also includes industrial automation companies such as Fanuc Corp. and Keyence Corp., alongside Nvidia and Intuitive Surgical Inc (NASDAQ:ISRG). This structure offers exposure to robotics adoption without making Tesla the dominant investment thesis.

Robotaxis Are Doing the Heavy Lifting

ARK’s forecast goes far beyond electric vehicle sales. The investment firm estimates robotaxis could account for approximately 80% of Tesla’s enterprise value by 2031.

Its base case projects 8.1 million robotaxis on the road and $753 billion in annual net ride-hailing revenue by 2031. It also anticipates roughly $212 billion in revenue from Optimus humanoid robots offered through a Robot-as-a-Service model.

These projections make autonomous driving and robotics important themes to examine when comparing ETFs. However, none of the three funds offers a direct claim on ARK’s projected Tesla returns.

The Risks Behind the ETF Trade

A slower robotaxi rollout, regulatory hurdles and delays in commercializing humanoid robots could undermine ARK’s assumptions. Even if Tesla advances these businesses, ETF investors may see different results depending on portfolio weights, other holdings, fees and broader market conditions.

For investors, the key distinction is between betting on Tesla’s valuation and investing in the technologies that could support its ambitions. ARKK and ARKQ provide substantial Tesla exposure, while BOTZ spreads its investments across a wider robotics ecosystem.

The bottom line is that ARK’s $4,400 Tesla forecast puts robotics and autonomous-driving ETFs on the radar, but the best measure of exposure is each fund’s actual holdings, not the upside implied by Tesla’s price target.

Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) remains in a technical correction, having fallen 18.8% from its peak earlier this month. The weakness coincides with an ongoing sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks, despite Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang dismissing memory glut fears.

Micron Technologies and other memory stocks have remained under pressure in the past few months. The Roundhill Memory ETF (CBOE: DRAM) has slumped more than 40% from its all-time high, while its outflows have surged. 

The ongoing weakness is partly because investors worry about a potential artificial intelligence bubble. Prominent figures like Ray Dalio, Ken Griffin, and Michael Burry have warned that the bubble may burst as interest rates rise. 

At the same time, concerns remain about a glut in the memory industry, since the sector is highly cyclical. In a statement today, Huang told CNBC that he saw no signs of a 2029 memory glut:

"We’re the first company in the world to put LPDDR memory — what goes into your cell phones — into the world’s data centers, and it’s enabled us to deliver performance that’s twice as energy efficient as anything in the world today, and so we’re going to continue to use abundant amounts of them as well."

In a separate statement, Huang said that demand in the AI infrastructure industry was strengthening. He cited the neocloud industry, where Nvidia has invested heavily in companies like CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV), IREN (NASDAQ:IREN), and Nebius (NASDAQ:NBIS). He said that demand for neocloud firms was "off the charts."

Micron’s Business is Seeing Strong Demand

The most recent earnings report showed that its revenue and profits surged in the fiscal fourth quarter. Revenue soared 379% to $54 billion, bringing the annual figure to $133 billion. Benzinga data shows analysts expect the revenue to jump to $275 billion this year and $318 billion in the next financial year. 

Demand for Micron is coming mostly from top hyperscalers, which are boosting their data center spending. In a report released last week, Gartner (NYSE:IT) predicted AI infrastructure spending will hit $1 trillion this year and add another $6 trillion between 2027 and 2030. Some of these funds will flow to Micron and other memory companies. 

Micron Stock is Undervalued, But Technical Risks Remain

Micron’s ongoing stock drop has made it look like a bargain by most metrics. Its forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio has fallen to 5.18, well below the technology sector median of 22 and its own five-year average of 74. Micron also has one of the highest Rule of 40 scores on Wall Street. Adding its revenue growth rate and its profit margin brings the score to about 170%.

The risk, however, is its technicals. It has dropped below the 100-day moving average and formed a bearish flag pattern. This pattern consists of a vertical line and a horizontal channel. In most cases, it leads to a strong bearish breakout that may push the stock to the $740 support level.

• Meta Platforms stock is taking a hit today. Why is META stock falling?

Meta shares fell more than 6% on Thursday after investors weighed stronger-than-expected revenue against rising artificial intelligence spending, a multibillion-dollar legal charge and a new $25 billion penalty in a data-privacy case. The stock had initially gained following the company’s third-quarter results. Reuters reported that the market was reassessing the cost of Meta’s AI ambitions despite progress in its business.

Why Meta Stock Is Under Pressure

Meta reported third-quarter revenue of $64.60 billion, up 26% year over year and ahead of analysts’ expectations. It also forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion, above the consensus estimate of $73.57 billion.

However, profitability and cash generation presented a more complicated picture.

The company recorded a $9.89 billion legal charge tied to its settlement with 52 state attorneys general over teen mental health litigation. Operating income fell 37% to $12.99 billion, while free cash flow turned negative at $2.12 billion.

Meta also raised its full-year capital expenditure outlook to $135 billion to $145 billion as it continues investing aggressively in AI infrastructure. Investors must weigh whether future AI-driven advertising growth and new products will generate sufficient returns to justify the spending.

Adding to the legal overhang, a New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion in a separate data-privacy case linked to allegations that the company misled users about its privacy practices.

How METQ Benefits From a Meta Sell-Off

METQ is designed to deliver 200% of the inverse of Meta stock’s daily performance, before fees and expenses. In practical terms, if META falls 1% over a trading day, METQ targets a gain of approximately 2%. If META rises 1%, the fund targets a loss of approximately 2%.

That makes the ETF a potential instrument for traders seeking short-term bearish exposure to Meta without directly shorting its shares. The fund resets its exposure daily, meaning its returns over multiple sessions can differ substantially from twice the inverse of META’s cumulative return.

For example, a 5% decline in META would imply a roughly 10% gain for METQ over that same day, assuming the fund meets its daily objective. Actual returns can differ because of expenses, market movements and tracking effects.

Price Analysis

METQ ETF shares were up 13.72% at $16.98 at the time of publication on Thursday, according to Benzinga Pro data. This notable increase indicates a strong bullish sentiment among traders, likely driven by recent volatility in the underlying Meta stock, which has been subject to significant market fluctuations.

The current price is positioned 6% below the key technical levels, suggesting that there is potential resistance around the $18 mark. This level has historically served as a psychological barrier, and breaking above it could signal a shift in momentum for METQ.

Trading volume on Thursday reached 1 million shares, reflecting heightened interest and activity in the ETF.

What Traders Should Watch Next

The immediate question is whether Meta’s post-earnings weakness persists or whether investors refocus on accelerating advertising revenue and the company’s AI initiatives, including its Muse products.

METQ’s performance will depend primarily on Meta’s daily share-price moves, rather than on whether the company’s long-term business outlook is improving or deteriorating. A rebound in Meta shares could quickly reverse gains in the inverse ETF.

The fund is therefore best understood as a high-risk, short-term trading vehicle rather than a straightforward way to express a long-term view on Meta. Its daily leverage can amplify losses as well as gains, and volatility can erode returns over longer holding periods.

Shares of Berkshire Hathaway Inc (NYSE:BRK)(NYSE:BRK) hit an all-time high on Wednesday, which may come as a surprise to those expecting lower returns after Warren Buffett stepped down as CEO and chairman of the conglomerate.

What’s Leading the Gains?

Berkshire Hathaway trailed the S&P 500, tracked by the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY), in 2025, closing out Buffett’s final year leading the company as CEO with a decline relative to the broader market.

There could be multiple reasons why investors are warming up to the Berkshire stock in a post-Buffett scenario.

The stock sold off earlier this year on his CEO exit and again on news that he was stepping down as chairman. Those declines came with the underlying businesses and investments still performing solidly.

The conglomerate’s second-quarter net earnings were $25.67 billion, more than double the $12.37 billion posted in the year-earlier period. Operating earnings, which include the underlying businesses, were up 16% year-over-year in the same quarter.

Along with the business strength, Berkshire Hathaway also bought back $4.5 billion of its own shares in the second quarter, a sign that the stock could be undervalued. The company also has a large cash balance, which could be put to work for more buybacks, acquisitions or to buy more stocks for the investment portfolio.

The firm’s investment portfolio could also be fueling investor enthusiasm, with its holdings offering a potential source of untapped value.

Here are the top 10 holdings as of the end of the second quarter and their year-to-date returns:

  • Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL): +26.9%
  • American Express (NYSE:AXP): -13.2%
  • Coca-Cola (NYSE:KO): +32.6%
  • Alphabet Class A (NASDAQ:GOOGL): +6.2%
  • Bank of America (NYSE:BAC): -9.2%
  • Chevron Corporation (NYSE:CVX): +45.5%
  • Occidental Petroleum (NYSE:OXY): +48.0%
  • Chubb Limited (NYSE:CB): +13.7%

Of the 10 positions, three are down and seven are up. Of the ones that are up, five are up double-digit percentages. Of the top 10 positions, the average return is a gain of 15.2% year-to-date.

That beats the current 13.1% year-to-date gain for the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust, meaning the top 10 stocks in the Berkshire Hathaway portfolio are outperforming the S&P 500 in 2026.

Changing of the Guard

With the change of CEO comes a learning curve and some uncertainties from long-time investors who were in Berkshire Hathaway due to Buffett.

New CEO Greg Abel has already begun reshaping Berkshire’s portfolio, with its first-quarter 13F filing showing the number of stock holdings fell from 42 to 29.

This included cutting long-time holdings like Visa and Mastercard and also exiting newer positions in UnitedHealth and Constellation Brands.

Not all of Abel’s stock picks will pay off, but his early portfolio changes and gains in retained holdings are rewarding investors who stayed the course.

Next up will be beating the S&P 500, which Buffett did in 13 of his last 25 years at the helm of Berkshire Hathaway and even more if you go back the decades before that.

Berkshire Hathaway stock is currently up 8.5% year-to-date, compared to the 13.1% gain for the SPY. Last year, the SPY outperformed Berkshire Hathaway with gains of 16.6% compared to 11.5%.

Meta beat third-quarter revenue estimates and guided higher, but lifted the low end of its 2026 capital expenditure forecast to $135 billion, from $130 billion.

CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV), the Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA)-backed neocloud company, faces significant debt stress as bond yields keep climbing amid ongoing fears of an artificial intelligence (AI) bubble. Its stock has also slipped to its lowest level since May last year. 

CoreWeave Bond Yields Are Rising

Investors are selling CoreWeave’s bonds as its debt continues to rise and jitters over the artificial intelligence industry intensify. The yield on its $2.75 billion bond maturing in 2031 rose to a record 15.76%, topping the previous high of 15.74% reached on October 14.

At the same time, the spread on its five-year credit default swaps (CDS) has risen 171% this year and 36% in the past month, reaching 1,115 basis points. A CDS is a form of insurance against default, so a rising spread signals that investors are paying more for protection.

The crisis has also spread to its stock, which continued its recent downward trend. It dropped to $56.50 on Thursday, down by 70% from its all-time high. Its market capitalization has dropped by $44 billion since May and $57 billion from its all-time high. 

The retreat has also hit other companies in the neocloud industry, with top companies like Nebius (NASDAQ:NBIS), IREN (NASDAQ:IREN), and RUM Group (NASDAQ:RUM) being in the red.

Read Also: Jensen Huang Downplays Memory Glut Fears: Will Micron Rebound Next?

Neocloud Industry is Facing Major Risks

CoreWeave and its competitors are facing substantial risks. Earlier this month, Firmus, another Nvidia-backed company, pulled its IPO in Australia as investors pushed back against its $30 billion valuation. Nscale, a similar company, is also facing investor pushback ahead of its IPO.

Gartner (NYSE:IT), a research firm, has warned that neocloud companies will be forced to announce large impairments in late 2030. The report cited the wide gap between ongoing AI spending and expected future revenue.

Indeed, CoreWeave has reported substantial depreciation and amortization costs this year. These rose to $2.5 billion in the first six months, compared with $4.6 billion in revenue. 

These concerns likely explain why CoreWeave’s insiders have continued selling shares. Benzinga data shows that top insiders have sold shares worth over $765 million in the last 90 days

Still, CoreWeave has some potential bullish catalysts. For one, demand for its services continues to rise, with its revenue backlog now over $104 billion. This backlog is from companies like Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Jane Street.

Further, Jensen Huang has maintained the view that neocloud companies are seeing strong demand. In a statement, he said that the demand was "off the charts", with the only limitation being working capital.

Blackstone Inc. (NYSE:BX) stock rose Thursday after the alternative asset manager reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings, although revenue missed Wall Street estimates.

Blackstone reported adjusted earnings of $1.32 per share, beating analysts’ consensus estimate of $1.26.

Revenue totaled $3.217 billion, below the $3.280 billion consensus estimate.

Blackstone Earnings Beat As Assets Reach Record $1.4 Trillion

Distributable earnings fell 9% year over year to $1.72 billion, reflecting lower investment realizations.

However, fee-related earnings increased 6% to $1.6 billion, or $1.26 per share. Total fee revenue rose 8% to $2.7 billion, while base management fees reached a quarterly record of $2 billion.

Transaction and advisory fees jumped 34% to $210 million. Meanwhile, fee-related performance revenue climbed 19% to $540 million, supported by 10 perpetual investment strategies.

Blackstone’s assets under management increased 10% year over year to a record of approximately $1.4 trillion.

The firm attracted $63 billion in quarterly inflows, bringing trailing 12-month inflows to more than $270 billion, the highest level in four years.

Net realizations declined 20% from the previous quarter, consistent with management’s expectations.

AI Infrastructure and Energy Investments Drive Expansion

Blackstone identified artificial intelligence infrastructure as a major growth opportunity, citing rising computing demand and shortages of data centers, electricity and equipment.

The firm launched Crux with Alphabet Inc.’s (NASDAQ:GOOGL) Google to address computing capacity shortages. It also partnered with Anthropic through ODE to accelerate enterprise AI adoption.

NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) selected Blackstone among a small group of investment managers to support $500 billion in GPU financing.

NVIDIA also made a strategic investment in Blackstone portfolio company Lancium to develop low-cost power infrastructure for OpenAI’s Texas data center.

Beyond AI computing, Blackstone is expanding investments in electricity generation, transmission, energy storage and related infrastructure.

Its credit business financed approximately 15% of U.S. solar and storage projects last year. Meanwhile, its credit and equity platforms supported nearly half of U.S. liquefied natural gas export capacity.

Third-quarter investments included a major European renewable energy developer and a supplier of data center cooling components.

During Thursday’s earnings call, CEO Stephen Schwarzman warned that accelerating AI computing demand is intensifying an already severe supply shortage. “Seldom in my career have I seen such a supply-constrained market of this scale,” Schwarzman said. He added that growing public opposition to data centers could further restrict supply, even as demand continues to surge.

See More: Top Momentum Stocks

Private Wealth Assets Climb to $330 Billion

Blackstone’s private wealth assets under management rose 15% year over year to a record $330 billion, supported by nearly $9 billion in quarterly sales.

BXP reached $29 billion in net asset value in less than three years, generating an 18% annualized net return since inception.

BREIT’s assets increased 9% to $58 billion, while regular-way net flows reached their strongest level in four years. Its largest share class delivered approximately 11% in net returns over the trailing 12 months.

BX Infra generated $1.1 billion in quarterly sales, lifting net asset value above $7 billion. Its largest share class posted a 17% annualized net return.

Meanwhile, BXHF raised approximately $400 million, including subscriptions received Oct. 1.

Blackstone also launched BXPM outside the United States and introduced investment products through partnerships with Wellington and Vanguard.

Private Credit Redemptions Offset Fundraising Growth

Blackstone’s insurance-channel assets increased 14% year over year to more than $300 billion across 40 clients.

Investment-grade private credit assets rose 24% to nearly $150 billion, while direct-lending assets increased 10% to almost $170 billion.

However, redemption pressures emerged in its flagship private credit vehicle, BCRED.

The fund generated nearly $750 million in third-quarter gross sales, but repurchase requests reached 10% of net asset value, twice its quarterly 5% limit.

Blackstone fulfilled approximately half of those requests, resulting in $1.4 billion in net outflows.

Institutional assets under management grew 7%, while the firm’s infrastructure platform expanded 40% to $97 billion. BXMA assets climbed 22% to $114 billion.

Blackstone also raised more than $16 billion toward its $22 billion secondaries fund target.

Its $8.7 billion BETP5 fund reached its fundraising ceiling, exceeding its predecessor’s size by more than 50%. A separate $4.2 billion asset-based finance vehicle is also approaching its fundraising limit.

The firm plans to launch a larger energy transition and infrastructure credit fund.

Blackstone Projects Stronger Fee Growth in 2027

Looking ahead, Blackstone expects base management fees to return to double-digit year-over-year growth in 2027.

The outlook reflects new private equity funds, expanding perpetual investment strategies and continued growth in credit, insurance and BXMA.

Management also expects net realizations to increase significantly in the fourth quarter, supported by planned portfolio company sales.

Additionally, BXMA and several credit strategies are expected to generate performance revenue from annual crystallization events.

Blackstone expects leasing activity across its global data center platform to triple in 2026. Data centers and logistics now account for 54% of its real estate portfolio.

However, management warned that geopolitical tensions, inflation, elevated oil prices, higher bond yields and uncertainty surrounding AI investment and private credit could weigh on markets.

The cost of insuring Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) debt against default rose to a record Thursday as investors weighed the Facebook parent’s growing AI spending plans.

Meta’s five-year credit default swaps rose 7.6 basis points to a record 114.79 basis points, according to Markit data cited by Reuters. 

The swaps work much like insurance on corporate debt, and a higher price means investors are paying more to protect against a default.

55 Billion in Bonds

Meta has sold $55 billion of bonds in the past year. It raised $30 billion in October 2025, its largest bond offering, and $25 billion more in April 2026.

On Wednesday, the company raised the low end of its 2026 capital spending forecast to $135 billion and kept the high end at $145 billion. 

Free cash flow was negative $2.12 billion in the third quarter, marking Meta’s first quarterly shortfall since 2012.

Meta also announced a new class of nonvoting Class C stock. According to Reuters, the company’s long-range forecasts call for raising hundreds of billions of dollars over several years to pay for its AI plans.

Cash Cushion

Meta is not close to default. It had $82.45 billion in cash and marketable securities as of Sept. 30, and third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.60 billion. 

Investors still want proof the spending will pay off.

"The market has been questioning whether all the spending on AI is having the type of returns that the market originally expected," Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers, told Reuters. 

Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC on Thursday that capital is tight across the AI industry. "The demand [for] the capital is much greater than the availability of the capital," he said.

Swaps on Oracle Corp. (NYSE:ORCL) also traded near a record, and those tied to Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) held near their highest level since March 2020, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence data cited by Reuters.
